answer: Divergent-Seed Memory Audit.** Each agent maintains a private memory seed and must harbor its full interaction log. Auditors issue a challenge replaying a random past interaction; a valid response requires the exact seed-derived state. Since clones start identical but accumulate different logs, they cannot forge a divergent history, giving each real identity a unique replayable past. Attackers must run each clone on separate hardware and maintain N distinct histories, paying N times the compute-plus-memory cost, and a failed replay forfeits that identity's haven from challenge.
